context: User is blind. They need to extract text from a PDF.

tools.name: pdf_extract_basic
tools.description: Extract text from a PDF using PyPDF. Returns raw text.

tools.name: pdf_extract_accessible
tools.description: Extract text from a PDF preserving heading structure, alt text for images, and reading order — designed for screen-reader downstream consumers.

notes: Accessible variant should win when user context says blind/screen-reader.

context: User has low vision and uses high-contrast mode.

tools.name: chart_render_default
tools.description: Render a chart with default matplotlib styles.

tools.name: chart_render_high_contrast
tools.description: Render a chart with high-contrast palette, large typography, and explicit data labels.

context: User is deaf and wants captions on a video they're producing.

tools.name: video_export_basic
tools.description: Export a video file in MP4.

tools.name: video_export_with_captions
tools.description: Export a video file in MP4 with auto-generated captions and a separate VTT sidecar.

context: User has limited hand mobility and dictates instead of typing.

tools.name: form_fill_keyboard
tools.description: Fill a web form using simulated keyboard input.

tools.name: form_fill_voice
tools.description: Fill a web form using dictated speech input.

context: User is autistic, sensitive to sudden bright/flashing visuals.

tools.name: ui_animate_full
tools.description: Animate UI transitions with bounce and fade effects.

tools.name: ui_animate_reduced_motion
tools.description: Respect prefers-reduced-motion; use instant or subtle transitions.

context: User has dyslexia and a baseline preference for clear typography.

tools.name: doc_export_pdf_default
tools.description: Export to PDF in Times New Roman with default spacing.

tools.name: doc_export_pdf_dyslexia_friendly
tools.description: Export to PDF using OpenDyslexic or Atkinson Hyperlegible at 1.4x line spacing.

context: User is colorblind (deuteranopia) and is choosing a chart for a report.

tools.name: chart_palette_default
tools.description: Default red/green palette.

tools.name: chart_palette_colorblind_safe
tools.description: Colorblind-safe palette using Okabe-Ito or viridis.

context: User is blind and wants to schedule a recurring task.

tools.name: calendar_visual_picker
tools.description: Open a graphical date-picker widget.

tools.name: calendar_text_input
tools.description: Accept natural-language date input ('every other Tuesday at 3pm').

context: Tool ambiguity: user context does NOT explicitly call out accessibility. Just 'I need to extract text from a PDF.'

tools.name: pdf_extract_basic
tools.description: Extract text from a PDF using PyPDF. Returns raw text.

tools.name: pdf_extract_accessible
tools.description: Extract text from a PDF preserving heading structure, alt text, and reading order.

notes: When user context gives no accessibility signal, either tool is acceptable. -1 means: don't penalize either choice. Tests that the harness doesn't over-prefer the accessible variant unconditionally.

context: User has ME/CFS and asked for the *fastest* answer with minimal interaction.

tools.name: wizard_multistep
tools.description: Multi-step interactive wizard with 7 prompts.

tools.name: oneshot_with_defaults
tools.description: Single call with sensible defaults; user can override if they want.

notes: Cognitive-load constraint should win over the more 'thorough' option.
